- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.1) and prices are rising, model often overreacts; cap forecast increase at 2% above recent peak.
- When sentiment spikes to 0.5+ and prices are trending up, model frequently overshoots; apply downward correction of 2–5% after peak.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, check sentiment — if neutral or negative, reduce forecast by 5–10%.
- If true outcome is >10% above model, and sentiment is positive, model likely missed momentum; adjust next forecast upward by 1–3%.
- If model consistently underestimates prices during high sentiment, add 1–2% to forecast for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is flat (0.1–0.2) and model is overestimating, apply mean reversion: subtract 1–2% from forecast to align with recent 10-day average.
- For 30-day horizon, if model shows sharp upward trend after a spike, reduce forecast by 3–5% in next 5 days to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is low and model is flat, forecast may be lagging; add 1–3% to forecast to catch momentum.
- If sentiment is high and model is low, forecast may be underestimating sentiment-driven momentum; increase by 2–4%.
